mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%) compresses equity discount rates and signals accommodative monetary policy, consistently producing positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as investors anticipate sustained liquidity support.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate increase (UNRATE > 5.5%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, prompting risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as corporate hiring slowdowns reduce earnings visibility.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based demand contraction, triggering profit margin concerns and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through reduced consumer spending confidence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: During supply-constrained regimes (INDPRO decline > 0.5% monthly), manufacturing bottlenecks and input cost pressures reduce corporate profitability, driving negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as margin compression intensifies.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: Positive month-over-month payroll growth (PAYEMS > 0) signals labor market strength, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which drives positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through sustained economic expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained consumer inflation spike (CPIAUCSL monthly change > 3.5%) triggers aggressive monetary tightening expectations, increasing equity discount rates and reducing valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP growth (GDPC1) signal severe economic contraction, triggering recession fears and negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns through accelerated earnings deterioration.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both INDPRO and GDPC1 decline.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market contraction (HOUST < 1000 thousand units) signals weak consumer demand for durable goods, causing immediate equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns through reduced near-term economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST falls below 1000.
